## Charles clean-up materials

**I. Kitchen**

a. Glass top oven cleaner, pads
b. Granite cleaner (counters)
c. Pine Sol (lemon scent) for floor
d. Mr. Clean spray cleaner (409 ok too) for cleaning refrig., cupboards, microwave etc.
e. Windex (for windows)
f. Sponge mop
g. Sponges, or wash cloths
h. Soft scrub for sink
i. Pledge, for woodwork, table, bar.
j. paper towels

**II. Main house**

a. Vacuum cleaner, cleaner bags
b. Broom
c. Windex for windows
d. Pledge for wood work (not for dining table)
e. Swiffer for dusting, and at least one replacement box

**III. Bedrooms**

a. Swiffer
b. Vacuum
c. Windex
d. Broom
e. Mop

**IV. Bathrooms**

a. Windex for mirrors
b. Comet for cleaning tub, sink,
c. mop,
d. Pine Sol
e. Sponges
f. Mr. Clean spray cleaner
g. Cleaning gloves
g. Toilet bowl (blue tablet cleaner)
h. Toilet bowl cleaning brush
i. Shower cleaner, spray

**V. Other items**

a. Fabreze air freshener

> *Note: Remember that it costs money to drive to the store, as well as your
> time is worth so much money. So get as big a supply as you can to save trips.*

## Charles House goals and fix-up

**I. Goals:**

A. I want to have a comfortable place to live and show hospitality that is neat, clean and enjoyable to be in.
B. I want to have free horizontal spaces
C. I want to show movies, entertain 8-10 people and if more use the cabana.
D. I want a hotel atmosphere

**II. Things to consider when looking at my condo.**

a. Lighting may include track, recessed, indirect, sconces, and skylights.
b. Artwork that is in keeping with the room and atmosphere that I am trying to create.
c. I want to create space by: the colors I choose, textures I use, lighting, furniture, and eliminate any objects that are cluttering my space.
d. I will find 1-3 proficient home decorators to help me to achieve my house goals. They will provide me with ideas that correlate with needs presented in this paper. I will have all measurements taken ahead of decorator's arrival. Discuss fireplace area and what can be done, and move bar or get rid of it.
e. What is the focal point of each room?

**III. Rooms thus far discussed.**

**A. Living room**

1. Possible skylights, better lighting. Make it light and open when wanted, can tone it down for evening use.
2. Touch up holes, cracks, maybe different color paint, or at least repainted.
3. Ceiling smoothed out and repainted. Possibly some ornate recessed work.
4. Possible different color for bay window.
5. Keep area rug
6. Coffee table/ glass over trunk
7. Possible side table behind couch
8. Sell pub table $150, chairs $87 each
9. Artwork that conveys feeling you want
10. If you get curtains, make light in color
11. Find out about using huge wall mirrors, or many squares to give light and make room feel bigger.

**B. Living room**

1. Lighting ok
2. Table ok
3. Possible change curtains to lighter ones that match kitchen cabinets.
4. Area rug under table.
5. Trash cans moved
6. Scrape and repaint ceilings
7. Talk to home decorator about mirror
8. Paint room
9. Reduce size of table when no company is around
10. Rearrange couches

**C. Kitchen**

1. Floor ok
2. Repaint walls
3. Possible aluminum siding over counters or something else
4. Scrape ceiling, repaint
5. Replace lighting to get more light, possible recess or more bulbs
6. Repaint cabinets white, reface, or other ideas
7. Take knobs off of drawers
8. Possibly take off sheetrock above cabinets
9. Replace end cabinet so that refrigerator can be moved over.
10. Appliances are good
11. Figure out trash can situation

**D. Bedroom**

1. New closet doors and inside (check with Dave and decorator for ideas.) Don't paint mirrors.
2. Repaint room
3. Scrape ceiling, repaint
4. Design better lighting for room
5. Take out book shelf and possible make it a divider for living and dining room.
6. Artwork
7. Chair ok, recover.
8. Get appropriate area rug
9. Redesign shower, possibly get a high quality unit or other ideas

**IV. Do list:**

A. Have mail sent to office
B. Take measurements of all the rooms
C. Find 1-3 house decorators that are competent
D. Get Dave or someone to sell pub table and chairs
E. Decide after talking to decorator about coffee and side table
F. Decide on trash cans
G. Decide where you are going to put current clutter and move it.
H. Possibly use bookshelf in bedroom to display cameras as a divider between living room and dining room. Use hall for bookshelf.
I. Check with board on skylights, or if can change rules.
J. Get ideas on better shower.
K. Assemble pub table for sale
L. Set date when you are going to start this due list and have it finished by. Have someone check you to see if you started and finished on time.

## Charles' Kitchen Clean-up

> *Received three times in the original email, identical each time. Preserved
> once here; the repetition is noted rather than reproduced.*

**I. Preface:**

**A.**

> **Memorize and apply the golden housekeeping rules: By following these rules
> you will save 50% of your time in taking care of your house. All of the
> following chores are to be done before going to bed. No bleeding heart, glazed
> eyes excuses that "I am tired", "I don't feel like it", "it doesn't really
> matter", "I will do it tomorrow". We are looking for preventative cleaning
> rather than crisis cleaning. God is a planner, a God of order and evolution
> isn't true. Your house will not go from chaos to order unless there is some
> planning and effort to keep it cleaned and organized.**
>
> **1. Everything has it's place.**
>
> **2. Do it now.**

**I. Preliminary: things that need to be done or asked.**

a. Do I really want to have a clean and organized kitchen and am I willing to work on it till the goal is reached?
b. Draw a diagram of what your cupboards or kitchen will look like.

**Things to purchase before starting**

a. Purchase spice racks or any other shelving that you will be using in your cupboards.
b. Purchase any shelf paper that you need.
c. Purchase cleaning agents, sponges, cleansers, gloves etc.

1. If you have a glass top stove you will need special cleaner
2. The sink can be cleaned with softsoap, or comet
3. Depending on your counters you can use special granite cleaner for granite, and Mr. Clean, or other spray cleaner for appliances, microwave, and counters.

## Provenance note

Recovered from Gmail 2026-09-19. Charles replied the same night: *"This is
awesome. Thanks."* Two days later he sent Dave a ChatGPT-generated mission
statement and ebook list built from these notes and asked *"Does this represent
what your lists could do for people? What's missing? What needs adjusting?"* —
the first recorded attempt at turning this into a product.

**Whose notes these are, settled:** they are **Dave's**, written *for* Charles,
addressed to Charles by name throughout ("Charles clean-up materials,"
"Charles' Kitchen Clean-up"). This resolves the open question in
[original-charles-cleanup-notes.md](original-charles-cleanup-notes.md).
